Nepal stands at a pivotal moment in its development journey. Over the 
past decades, the country has made notable progress in consolidating 
peace, advancing federalism, expanding representation, and improving 
access to services. The promulgation of the 2015 Constitution and 
subsequent institutional reforms have laid the foundations for a more 
inclusive, accountable, and citizen-centric state. These achievements 
reflect the sustained commitment of the Government of Nepal and the 
resilience of its people. 
At the same time, Nepal’s aspirations for inclusive, resilient, and sustainable 
development require continued progress in strengthening governance 
systems and public sector management. The government’s ongoing 
reform momentum, including policies and priorities such as its 100-point 
agenda for reform and 16th Five-Year Plan, signals a strong recognition that
